title: bug: Read-only Agent fanout leaks raw reports and session artifacts
description:
## Pi version

0.83.0

## Pi Stuff version or commit

0.1.0 (current behavior; originally observed in a pre-release dogfood checkout)

## What happened

A read-only repository review delegated to three background Agents produced a normal synthesized review, then injected a visible numbered dump of all three child reports into the main conversation. The dump repeated findings, exposed child execution-limit commentary, truncated one report in the middle of a finding, and triggered another main-Agent response without new user input.

The same fanout wrote about 3.6 MB of Agent-owned session artifacts into the clean repository. Those files appeared in Git status, and the review then reported its own artifact directory as a missing-ignore-rule problem.

## What I expected

A fanout should produce one coherent, bounded user-facing completion from the main Agent. Raw child reports and operational details should remain inspectable through `/agents`, without a duplicate follow-up turn after the results have already been synthesized.

Read-only delegation should also leave the reviewed repository unchanged. Suite-owned session evidence must not become content that the delegated review evaluates or require every repository to add a Suite-specific ignore rule.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start a Suite-enabled Pi session in a clean Git repository.
2. Ask the main Agent to review the repository with several background Agents and explicitly prohibit edits.
3. Let the main Agent continue its own review and synthesize the child findings.
4. Wait for background completion delivery.
5. Inspect the main conversation and Git status.

## Additional context

Observed in dogfood session `019fc891-1fd3-74d8-b39f-a700b06b2be0`. The completion payload was neither a compact summary nor a complete report, and different children disagreed on whether the Agent-owned artifacts were repository content.

title: bug: Todo checklist displays contextless blocker metadata
description:
## Pi version

0.83.0

## Pi Stuff version or commit

0.1.0

## What happened

When a Todo task has an unresolved dependency, the expanded checklist above the editor dims the task and appends text such as `blocked by #1`.

The checklist does not otherwise show task IDs, and its five-row limit may omit the referenced task. At narrow widths, the blocker label is preserved while the task subject is shortened or removed, so the least actionable information can replace the actual plan.

## What I expected

The bounded Todo checklist should prioritize each task's subject and status. Contextless blocker IDs are not useful in this user-facing surface and should not displace the task subject; dependency details can remain available to the Agent through the Task tools.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start an interactive Host session with the Suite loaded.

3. Add the first task as a dependency of the second with `TaskUpdate`.
4. Observe `blocked by #1` in the expanded checklist above the editor.
5. Narrow the terminal and observe that the blocker label survives while the task subject is progressively truncated.

## Additional context

This concerns the normal expanded Todo widget. Completing or deleting the dependency correctly removes it from the unresolved blocker state.

4. Real Pi 0.83 PTY acceptance at 100x32 and 64x28, including CJK, resize, deterministic focus restoration, and long-session behavior.

## Sequencing rule

## Boundaries

The prior prohibition still applies to capability-specific Agent, Todo, Fleet, health, Goal, scheduler, Memory, and MCP status rows. Command Dialog focus hides the footer and restores the exact previous footer on close.

Tool presentation follows summary to detail to action. Consecutive low-impact exploration may collapse semantically; consequential operations remain individually legible. One operation updates in place through running and terminal states. Errors and rejections stay attached to the operation. Local details replace the focused region and return with Esc; global expansion is not the normal path.

Claude Code remains the primary observable information-hierarchy and interaction reference. Pi public APIs, theme tokens, SettingsList, keybindings, and real PTY behavior remain implementation authority.

title: Remove the Magic Context first-prompt TUI stall
description: In a long resumed Pi session, submitting the first prompt can leave the editor visibly frozen because Pi Stuff awaits the initial Magic Context module load and activation on the input event. After activation, the long-history Context transform can also occupy the event loop before the already-requested user-message/working render is painted.
design: Keep the pinned official Magic Context core unmodified and do not fork Pi. Start and await only its pure JavaScript module load while Pi Stuff capabilities initialize, before the editor is presented; keep the Magic factory, SQLite setup, migrations, and session replay user-triggered. Preserve Pi native editor submission exactly. Only when the Context Capability receives an interactive input, request a normal incremental render and yield one 60 Hz frame before Magic activation. Before the first Context transform for that input, request and yield one further frame so the user message and working state can paint. Slash commands handled before Context, RPC, extension input, non-Context use, and tool-only Context passes receive no added submission delay.
acceptance_criteria: On repeated real Pi 0.83 PTY runs at 100x32 and 64x28 using a resumed session with at least 1,000 messages: (1) cold and warm Enter-to-editor-clear/first-paint p95 is no more than 25 ms slower than an otherwise identical true no-Context arm; (2) the official Magic module is no longer first imported under the input handler; (3) no Magic database or state is created or mutated merely by extension load or session_start; (4) provider messages, transformed Context, compaction ownership, resume behavior, and automatic overflow protection remain unchanged; and (5) no Pi core or upstream Magic Context source is modified.
notes:
Diagnosis on 2026-08-06: with the current long resumed session, the first input handler/agent event waited about 0.66–0.74 s, dominated by the first dynamic import. The first Magic transforms took about 0.33 s and 0.22 s; steady transforms were about 42–53 ms. A true no-Context arm reached agent start in about 2–4 ms warm. Real PTY first paint was about 1.13 s with current lazy loading versus about 56–81 ms without Context. Preloading only the module reduced cold agent start to about 73 ms. A throwaway forced-render prototype reduced warm visible acknowledgement from about 48 ms to about 16 ms, while a one-frame yield allowed the terminal to paint before the transform. Auto-search and log routing were not primary causes.
Implemented and certified on 2026-08-06. The final design rejected forced full redraw because it needlessly repainted long transcripts. On a real resumed Pi 0.83 session with 1,548 messages, 100x32 Enter acknowledgement was 12.541 ms median / 19.465 ms p95 with Pi Stuff versus 12.275 / 13.594 ms for the identical Suite without Context: +0.266 ms median / +5.871 ms p95. At 64x28 it was 13.308 ms median / 15.071 ms p95; median delta from no-Context was +0.368 ms. The first Magic provider handoff still performs user-triggered session initialization, about 0.62-0.72 s in this long fixture, but only after the editor and working UI have painted. A real startup-only Pi run proves extension load and session_start create no Magic database. Real Context PTY verifies transformed provider context, manual and automatic compaction ownership, resume, project isolation, native-compaction adoption and fail-open. Full source test result: 632 passed, 0 failed; Goal upstream, typecheck, knip, generated/public safety and certified package checks passed. Current settings-based RPC smoke loaded the repository source directly with no pi-stuff-current indirection.
2026-08-06 follow-up review: the editor-level 17 ms timer is broader than necessary because it delays every submission, including slash commands and non-Context input, and leaves a theoretical stale-callback window across reload or shutdown. Refine the handoff so only interactive Context input requests the first paint/frame; keep the later pre-transform frame for the user-message/working state.
Follow-up refinement completed on 2026-08-06. Removed the editor-level timer entirely, so ordinary prompts and /ui are handed to the Pi Host synchronously and no delayed callback can survive reload or shutdown. The red-capable tests first demonstrated both old defects, then passed after moving the first frame into interactive Context input. On the same 1,548-message session, final Pi Stuff acknowledgement was 10.894 ms median / 11.343 ms p95 at 100x32 and 10.757 / 11.022 ms at 64x28. The Suite-without-Context arm now remains native at 43.325 / 74.754 ms and 47.134 / 75.998 ms respectively, confirming it no longer receives the UI timer. Real Pi UI and Context PTYs passed; 631 source tests passed with zero failures, the one RTK environment test remained skipped, and all Goal upstream tests passed.
close_reason: Final refinement preserves native submission for every non-Context path while keeping approximately 11 ms visible acknowledgement for long interactive Magic Context turns; regression, wide/narrow PTY and full-suite tests passed.

title: Restore compact Tool rows across session resume
description: In-process /resume rebuilds historical tool rows with Pi raw renderers. The same history becomes compact after /reload, and direct fresh-process --session startup is already compact. The current real-PTY gate covers live calls and /reload but not in-process /resume.
design: Fix inside the Suite without forking Pi. Carry a bounded, consume-once active-builtin handoff across session replacement so the incoming Extension factory can install presentation definitions before historical reconstruction. At session_start, re-register against the target cwd and trust/settings context and restore exact active-tool membership. Do not globally pre-register all built-ins because that can revive grep/find/ls or violate explicit disabled/allowlisted configurations.

title: Align BTW with the confirmed concise side-question contract
description:
## Purpose

Bring BTW to the confirmed concise Claude-style information structure while preserving Pi Stuff's already accepted Suite container and Pi Host boundary. Claude Code 2.1.220 is observable behavior and visual evidence only; its code is not implementation input, and pixel-for-pixel reproduction is not the target.

## Confirmed scope

- Change only the BTW Capability. Do not change the shared Command Dialog contract or other Capabilities.
- Keep the full-width non-floating Pi Stuff Command Dialog, Pi-native theme tokens, the Answering spinner, blocking-surface preemption, and exact editor/footer/working-row/Suite-chrome restoration.
- The focused content is only `/btw <question>`, the streamed Markdown answer, and context-sensitive shortcut hints.
- Remove the visible `BTW`, `Question`, `Answer`, `single exchange`, `side question · main task continues`, and earlier-exchange explanatory labels.
- Use Claude Code 2.1.220 as the reference for concise information hierarchy, not as a second Host, copied implementation, or exact terminal-cell skin.

## Confirmed behavior

- Match Claude's published non-UI behavior by default: one no-tool answer outside the main transcript, independent cancellation, selected history, copy, clear, and explicit promotion through `f`.
- Support context-sensitive `f`, history navigation, copy, clear, Space, Enter, and Esc controls. Unknown edge behavior is conservative: do not mutate the original session or expose data implicitly.
- Promotion waits for the main Agent to become idle, then opens a new session in which the selected BTW question and answer are formal user and assistant turns. The original session remains unchanged.
- BTW context includes completed main text, images, tool results, and compaction-aware context. It excludes an unfinished assistant partial.
- Successful BTW history is local to the original session and survives resume for that session's lifetime. `/clear` and ordinary branch/fork creation do not inherit it. The user should experience it as session-lifetime history; only an abnormal size bound may evict the oldest entries.
- The earlier `f` record means a confirmed long-term target. Its omission from the first implementation tranche was a deferral, not an open product decision and not a rejection.
- Pi 0.83's missing transcript-free Host model-call seam remains tracked separately and does not block this work. Do not fork Pi and do not weaken transcript isolation.

## Delivery boundary

Phase 1 records this contract and produces disposable native Pi/Bun TUI evidence at 100×32 and 64×28 plus a concise comparison report. Production BTW changes require explicit approval after the prototype review.
design:
## UI states

1. Answering: `/btw <question>`, a Pi-themed Answering spinner, and `Esc cancel`.
2. Answered: the same question, Markdown answer, and only the actions currently available for the selected exchange.
3. History: compact prior `/btw` questions with one selected answer; no separate explanatory panel or redundant headings.

## Acceptance boundary

- Real Pi 0.83 Host and Bun 1.3.14, not a GUI/browser mock.
- Reference and proposed frames at both 100×32 and 64×28.
- No floating overlay, statusline, normal-screen BTW row, or copied Claude source.
- Phase 1 may add only research/prototype/report files and this Bead. It must not edit production BTW code.
acceptance_criteria: Phase 1 records the canonical contract and supplies reproducible native Pi 0.83/Bun 1.3.14 answering, answered, and history evidence at 100x32 and 64x28 plus a concise Claude/current/proposed HTML comparison. No production BTW file changes before maintainer approval. Phase 2 must implement the accepted UI, controls, session-lifetime local history, completed-context semantics, and idle-safe promotion with focused tests while preserving the shared Command Dialog and no-Pi-fork boundary.
notes:
Phase 2 completion evidence (2026-08-02)

Implemented the accepted concise BTW contract in packages/pi-stuff-btw: full-width non-floating Command Dialog; /btw question, native Answering loader, streamed Markdown answer, compact five-row history window with all exchanges navigable; c/x/f plus Space/Enter/Esc and Kitty printable-key decoding; no redundant BTW/Question/Answer/explanatory labels. Durable invisible session-owned history resumes in the original session and does not enter model context or inherit into a promoted/new session. Context preserves completed text, images, tool calls/results, and compaction context while excluding pending assistant partials. f waits for main idle, promotes the selected Q/A as formal turns in a new session, leaves the original transcript unchanged, and makes no extra model request.

Equivalence wording: this matches the confirmed Claude Code side-question user effect and concise information hierarchy; it intentionally does not claim pixel-for-pixel identity or copying of Claude private implementation. Pi theme tokens, divider, loader, viewport behavior, and the shared Suite Command Dialog remain Pi-native. Genuine Claude Code 2.1.220 captures and actual production Pi frames are compared in docs/prototypes/tui/work-btw-phase1-report.html.

Verification: 23 focused core/history/UI tests pass; real Pi 0.83 Host load passes; the real PTY gate passes at 100x32 and 64x28, covering concurrent main/BTW streaming, tools=[], formal-transcript isolation, draft/focus restoration, durable resume, session isolation, promotion/session switch, dialog cleanup, and exactly two model requests. The genuine 2.1.220 probe confirms Space, Enter, and Esc cancel the pending Answering surface. Six production captures live under docs/prototypes/tui/artifacts/pi-0.83-btw-phase2-production-*.png. Pi 0.83 host-managed transcript-free provider lifecycle remains separately tracked by ps-5cb.3.
close_reason: Accepted BTW Phase 1 and Phase 2 contract, production implementation, genuine-Claude comparison, focused tests, real Host verification, and 100x32/64x28 real-PTY gates are complete; the upstream Host seam remains separately tracked by ps-5cb.3.

title: Define the Pi Stuff product capability set
description:
## Purpose

Decide which user-visible capabilities belong in the default Pi Stuff installation before selecting upstream Pi Packages or implementing any Capability.

This epic records the product interview, confirmed decisions, open questions, Package research, and final inclusion/exclusion decisions. It does not authorize implementation.

## Confirmed decisions

1. Pi Stuff is personal-first. It may remain publicly usable, but it is selected for the maintainer's own daily workflow rather than for every possible Pi user.
2. A third-party capability may be adopted only through an owned fork whose source is incorporated into the Pi Stuff monorepo as part of the Suite. Direct dependence on the original Package is not the target model.
3. Owned forks preserve upstream provenance, the upstream revision, applicable licenses, and a visible record of local changes. Product direction and release timing belong to Pi Stuff; low divergence from upstream is not a goal by itself.
4. The previous `jczhang02/pi-agent` repository is evidence for capability inventory and user experience only. Its code must not be copied, ported, translated, or otherwise used as implementation input.
5. A normal Pi Stuff installation should be immediately useful with a coherent default set of features, without requiring the user to enable and configure each one first.
6. Additional agents may be started automatically when useful; the user should not have to request every delegation manually.
7. Product decisions must be discussed through concrete usage scenarios and plain language. Unexplained implementation or product jargon is not an acceptable decision interface.
8. Large capability directions must be chosen before detailed UI behavior, Package selection, or implementation planning.

## Open decisions

- Which large user-visible capability directions belong in Pi Stuff?
- Which concrete daily workflows should each direction enable?
- Which directions are part of the default installation, optional, or excluded?
- Which existing Pi Packages are credible candidates for each accepted direction?
- Which candidate should be forked after comparing actual behavior, maintenance, adoption, license, compatibility, and source quality?
- What user experience should unify the selected forks?

## Process

1. Resolve one user decision at a time using concrete scenarios.
2. Append every confirmed decision to this epic.
3. Research facts rather than asking the user to supply them.
4. Search and compare Pi Packages only after the corresponding large capability direction is accepted.
5. Do not create implementation work until the user confirms that the product set is understood.
acceptance_criteria: Confirmed large capability directions, default/optional/excluded choices, candidate Package comparisons, fork selections, and unresolved questions are recorded; the user explicitly confirms shared understanding before implementation work is created.
notes:
Confirmed 2026-08-01 — Work-process management belongs in the default installation. During long work, Pi Stuff must show current, pending, blocked, and completed tasks; let the user add, cancel, or reorder work; answer BTW side questions without stopping the main task; continue owned work in the background; and notify the user when work completes or needs input.
Confirmed 2026-08-01 — UI quality is a first-class default product direction, not merely a consistency layer for new Pi Stuff features. Pi Stuff may substantially reshape any user-visible presentation reachable without forking or modifying Pi itself, including built-in tool-call/result display, transcript presentation, diffs, test and error output, status/footer areas, Agent and task views, commands, and settings screens. The non-negotiable boundary is that Pi remains the Host and Pi core is not forked.
Confirmed 2026-08-01 — Cross-session project and work memory belongs in the default installation. On returning to a repository, Pi Stuff should retain useful commands, important structure and conventions, prior investigations and failed approaches, user preferences, unfinished work, and key decisions preserved through long-conversation compression. Remembered information must be visible to the user and support correction and deletion.
Confirmed 2026-08-01 — End-to-end development work belongs in the default installation. Given a concrete issue, Pi Stuff should be able to read the issue and discussion, investigate and modify code, run the project's tests/lint/typecheck/build, inspect its own diff, obtain an additional-agent review, prepare commit and pull-request text, and inspect and repair CI failures. Commit, push, and pull-request creation still require the user's explicit request.
Confirmed 2026-08-01 — Internet research belongs in the default installation. When a task depends on current or external facts, Pi Stuff should search primary sources, read official documentation, release notes, GitHub material, web pages, PDFs, and relevant downloaded files, show important source links to the user, and use the verified information in subsequent work. It should not perform unnecessary network research for every task.
Confirmed 2026-08-01 — Internet reading and external-service connections are one large default product direction, not separate directions. This area covers searching and reading web sources and documents, working with GitHub and other connected services, querying external systems and internal tools, and performing authorized actions through those connections. Account-specific connections remain user-selected and are not silently enabled.
Product-boundary correction: Do not promote tasks that an agent can already accomplish by composing ordinary tools into separate Pi Stuff capability areas. Web reading, operating external services, release routines, recurring checks, and similar examples are tool-enabled behaviors unless they require distinct product infrastructure, persistent state, coordination semantics, or user-facing control. The capability map must describe product mechanisms Pi Stuff itself adds, not an inventory of jobs the model may claim it can perform.
Reclassification after product-boundary correction: 'Internet research and external-service connections' are not standalone claimed Agent capabilities; they belong under one Tool and Connection layer that supplies concrete tools. The proposed 'reusable/automatic routines' question is withdrawn because its examples can be achieved by an Agent composing tools. The earlier 'end-to-end development workflow' entry is also provisional and must be re-audited under the same rule: an outcome or workflow is not automatically a Pi Stuff product block. Future grilling will first classify mechanisms (orchestration, persistent state, interaction/UI, tools, etc.) and ask only about real product tradeoffs.
Confirmed 2026-08-01 — The product map uses five mechanism-level blocks: (1) multi-Agent system; (2) work and conversation control, including Todo, BTW, and background work; (3) unified UI; (4) context and long-term continuity; and (5) tools and external connections. Blocks 1–3 form the product center; blocks 4–5 support that center. Pi Host facilities and source/fork/package governance are foundations rather than feature blocks. Only mechanism-level choices are grilled; Package facts are researched, and tool-composed tasks are acceptance scenarios rather than feature names.
Multi-Agent Package research snapshot, 2026-08-01 —  v0.38.0 is MIT, reports about 166k npm downloads/month, has active cross-platform CI and the broadest directly usable delegation/background/persistence/control surface, but carries roughly 56k lines of TypeScript plus a comparably large test base and needs explicit Pi 0.83 certification.  v0.14.3 is MIT, reports about 43.6k downloads/month, has a smaller roughly 9.2k-line TypeScript surface and a strong controllable-Agent UI, but a local Pi 0.83 dependency check exposed a type error and its persistent-background guarantees are weaker.  is a much larger workflow/team platform whose author warns that most code was AI-generated with limited line-by-line human review;  adds a general programmable tool/Agent runtime that conflicts with Pi remaining the Host;  currently lacks a clear redistribution license and relies on a narrow Pi runtime patch. Download counts are adoption signals only, not user counts. Product-shape choice must precede final fork selection.
Correction to the immediately preceding research snapshot: the package names omitted there are, in order, pi-subagents, @tintinweb/pi-subagents, pi-crew, pi-fabric, and claude-style-subagent. This correction preserves the original audit trail and supplies the missing identifiers.
Confirmed 2026-08-01 — The multi-Agent block uses the assistant model: the user remains in one main Pi conversation; the main Agent may automatically delegate to child Agents; child work is visible and the user can inspect, enter, redirect, stop, or continue it. A separate team/workflow engine is not the foundation of this block.
Multi-Agent candidate jury, 2026-08-01 — Three independent reviews plus maintainer verification agree on a split result. Capability: pi-subagents wins because it provides detached child processes, durable lifecycle records, recovery and resume, acknowledged control, failure handling, worktree handoff, and versioned extension seams. UI: @tintinweb/pi-subagents wins because its Fleet to live conversation to inline steer and two-step stop path is more direct and discoverable, with a more coherent Agent and settings hub. Both pass their pinned upstream test baselines. Against Pi 0.83, pi-subagents has six failures isolated to its optional watchdog adapter while its core real-session E2E passes; @tintinweb/pi-subagents has a type incompatibility in the core Agent session creation path. Recommended pending user confirmation: fork pi-subagents as the capability kernel, initially expose only single and parallel assistants plus visible status, conversation inspection, steer, stop, and resume; keep chain, scheduling, watchdog, memory, profiles, and sharing outside the first public surface. Rebuild the Pi Stuff unified UI toward the better interaction behavior observed in @tintinweb/pi-subagents without adopting or copying that Package code. The principal cost is ownership of the much larger pi-subagents codebase.
Confirmed 2026-08-01 — Pi Stuff will use an owned fork of nicobailon/pi-subagents as the capability basis for the multi-Agent block. @tintinweb/pi-subagents is a reference for observable UI behavior only; its code is not adopted or copied. Upstream pi-subagents UI features have no default preservation requirement: Pi Stuff will retain, replace, hide, or remove them only according to the later unified-UI design. Selecting the capability fork does not let the upstream Package define the Suite UI.
Work-and-conversation-control research snapshot, 2026-08-01 — Pi 0.83 already owns steering, follow-up queues, cancellation, session persistence and branching, compaction, and the UI extension containers; Pi Stuff should reuse those facilities rather than fork substitutes. Pi still lacks product-level Todo, isolated concurrent BTW conversation, and background-job management. For session Todo, @juicesharp/rpiv-todo is the leading fork candidate: roughly 29k monthly downloads, MIT, Pi 0.83 typecheck and 224 tests passed, branch-aware recovery and dependency validation; its upstream UI need not be preserved. Project-level Todo packages are disfavored because they duplicate Beads. For BTW, the leading bounded candidate is @narumitw/pi-btw: roughly 7.3k monthly downloads, MIT, Pi 0.83-compatible, genuinely concurrent and context-isolated but intentionally without file or shell tools. pi-btw is also mature and concurrent but is effectively another tool-capable Agent, overlapping the selected pi-subagents fork. Package selection remains pending the corresponding product-boundary decisions.
Confirmed 2026-08-01 — Todo is a session-scale view of the current piece of work, not a second project tracker. It shows current, pending, blocked, and completed items; the user may add, cancel, or reorder them; and the state should survive reload, conversation compaction, and session recovery. Long-lived issues, decisions, acceptance criteria, and work that must remain for later belong in Beads. Todo does not maintain a separate project backlog or automatically synchronize bidirectionally with Beads. @juicesharp/rpiv-todo is the explicit reference candidate for this capability; whether it is adopted as the owned-fork base or used only as behavior reference remains to be confirmed.

The circuit breaker must run before unrestricted mode, project/Agent/session rules, child policy, and external authorizers; project content cannot weaken it. comments.author: JC Zhang
comments.text: Source-backed UI recommendation pending maintainer confirmation, 2026-08-01 — Claude Code evidence supports three distinct reading layers: the default conversation is optimized for understanding, the detailed transcript is optimized for inspection while still filtering noise, and a separate durable session record is optimized for recovery and export. Visible content is classified by human meaning rather than provider message role. One tool or foreground-Agent operation owns its queued, waiting, running, success, failure, rejected, and canceled states; live progress updates that record in place. Consecutive low-impact exploration may collapse into a semantic activity summary, while edits, other consequential mutations, failures, and user-action requirements must remain visible. Successful internal helper tools may render nothing, and duplicate expressions of the same fact should have one visible owner. Foreground Agent work leaves a compact expandable operation record. Background work uses a compact launch record, temporary near-editor running status, an Agents or Tasks Command Dialog for full control, and one terminal completion, failure, stop, or needs-input summary in the main conversation. Todo state and routine Todo updates do not enter the transcript. BTW lives in its Command Dialog and may keep session-local BTW history, but never enters the main conversation. Informational system noise and recovered retries disappear; user-affecting warnings, errors, compaction, interruption, recovery, and permission outcomes remain. Exact visuals and line budgets are intentionally not decided here. Evidence is recorded in docs/research/claude-code-transcript-source-decisions.md; the source provenance and no-copy boundary remain in force.

comments.author: JC Zhang
comments.text: Feasibility correction and recommendation pending maintainer confirmation, 2026-08-01 — Semantic grouping is not a native Pi 0.83 transcript facility. Without forking Pi, it is feasible only as a Pi Stuff-owned projection: collect consecutive calls from owned or overridden read-only tools, hide their individual transcript rows, and append one persistent summary. Arbitrary third-party or MCP tools cannot be transparently grouped while retaining an execution implementation Pi Stuff does not own. The first bounded scope should be read, grep, find, ls, and owned web-reading tools; mutations, side-effecting commands, failures, rejections, and user-action requirements stay separate. This is medium-complexity state, persistence, and rendering work rather than a styling tweak. Pi 0.83 Ctrl+O is one global boolean and rerenders every expandable historical child; there is no public per-row transcript focus or selective inline expansion API. Recommended combined direction: keep the main transcript permanently bounded and use a Tool Details Command Dialog for full content. Ctrl+O would open the latest group or operation, let the user select one constituent operation and scroll only that output, then Esc back to the unchanged transcript. This can be implemented without a Pi fork through public custom-UI APIs; using Ctrl+O requires an explicit Pi Stuff keybinding change that removes the Host global-expand binding before registering the focused inspector. Exact appearance and controls require a real Pi PTY preview before confirmation.

comments.author: JC Zhang
comments.text: Confirmed 2026-08-02 — Safe recovery belongs in the default Pi Stuff installation as the second half of the safety-and-recoverability block. Recovery is automatic and quiet: each user request establishes a recognizable recovery point without requiring a manual save. From a prior request, the user can restore Agent-made local code changes only, conversation only, or both; recovery survives session resume and compaction, previews affected files, preserves pre-existing and later user edits, stops on ambiguous conflicts instead of silently overwriting them, and creates an undo point before applying a restore. Conversation branching remains available when the user wants to preserve the current route and try another. Recovery does not claim to reverse external APIs, databases, deployments, or other remote side effects; those remain governed before execution by the separate safety policy. Unlike current Claude Code, Pi Stuff must not silently leave background subagent edits outside the product promise: writing Agents must either participate in a defined recovery domain or work in isolation that can be discarded safely. Healthy checkpointing adds no statusline or persistent UI. Exact panel layout and keys remain later UI decisions and require a real Pi/HTML preview under the established UI process.

comments.text: Confirmed safety behavior, 2026-08-02 — The maintainer chooses an unrestricted-working default with a safety backstop, now mapped to current Claude Code Auto behavior rather than YOLO/bypassPermissions. Routine reads, edits and ordinary commands inside the current workspace proceed without approval; safe read-only network use and already-authorized connections also proceed. One central pre-action policy covers built-in file/shell tools, owned-fork tools, MCP calls and every foreground/background subagent. Actions outside the workspace or against external/shared state—destructive deletion, force push/protected branch, production deploy/migration, permissions/IAM, mass cloud deletion, secret transmission, or unknown infrastructure—are blocked for a safe alternative or routed to a bounded safety review using the user request, project instructions and proposed action but no untrusted tool output. Only when the action is still necessary and the user did not already give exact authority does the shared non-floating Command Dialog ask. Explicit user boundaries such as do-not-push are treated as blocks, but durable deny rules—not transcript memory—provide hard guarantees. The default is not a claim of perfect safety. Healthy safety infrastructure has no statusline; denials are visible with reason and can be reviewed/retried. OS-level workspace/network sandboxing should be used where available and must fail visibly to policy review rather than silently disappearing. Exact owned-fork base and runtime gates remain under package audit.

Pi Stuff adds no persistent health, Goal, scheduler, memory, MCP, Fleet or Agent statusline. Goal evaluator outcomes are short transcript events; BTW/scheduled/runtime management occupies zero rows while closed.

Use the same full-width divider-led non-floating Command Dialog primitive for runtime `/tasks`, `/goal`, scheduled work, BTW history and Agent detail, while keeping their authorities and commands separate. First line divider; quiet title/scope/count; one selection marker; Enter replaces list with detail in the same region; Esc returns detail→list→close; close restores editor text/widgets/Host footer. description: BTW history currently clears and persists immediately from one x keypress, with no confirmation or recovery.
design: If approved, keep the same full-width surface and switch to an inline confirmation state: Clear earlier BTW history? y confirm and Esc cancel. Do not add a floating modal.
acceptance_criteria: A user cannot irreversibly clear earlier BTW history with one accidental keypress; confirm, cancel, persistence failure, resize, resume, and draft restoration are verified.
notes:
Implemented inline two-step confirmation in the existing full-width BTW Command Dialog: x enters confirmation, y commits, Esc/n cancels; no overlay or floating surface.
Maintainer approved the inline confirmation. Signed commit e2b33e7 verifies x to ask, y to clear, Esc/n to cancel, persistence, fork, resume, both accepted widths, and exact draft restoration in real Pi.
close_reason: Implemented, tested through source and certified release artifacts, installed as Pi Stuff 0.3.2, and reverified in real Pi TUI.

title: Add direct user control for session Todo
description: Record the remaining product gap between the shipped session Todo and the earlier user-control goal. The current Todo is stable and useful: Agent tools create and update session work, state survives the supported session lifecycle, and the bounded checklist accurately projects that state. What is not yet shipped is a user-facing way to add an item, cancel an item, or change ordering directly.
design: Keep Todo session-scoped and distinct from Beads. Add direct management through the shared full-width non-floating Command Dialog or another equally concrete Pi-native path. Preserve the bounded normal checklist and the current Agent tools. The current Ctrl+Shift+T binding only toggles visibility; it is not a broken reorder binding. A future shortcut must be selected after a Host and Suite conflict audit, remain discoverable, and be configurable rather than hard-coded.
acceptance_criteria: From a normal session the user can add a Todo item, cancel an unfinished item, and reorder unfinished items without asking the Agent to issue a tool call. Changes immediately update the one canonical Todo state, survive reload and compaction under existing rules, and never create or synchronize a project backlog. Existing Agent tool behavior remains compatible. The management command, keyboard hints, empty state, cancellation semantics, ordering rules, and final shortcut are covered at 100x32 and 64x28 with focus and draft restoration. Documentation explicitly describes this as an added product surface, not a repair for a broken current Todo.
close_reason: Superseded by the later maintainer decision: direct Todo add, cancel and reorder UI is not required. Keep the bounded Agent-owned list and visibility control.

title: Build the production local Memory Capability
description: After the disposable prototype passes, ship cross-session project Memory as an owned Pi Stuff Capability Package. The Capability recalls only a small relevant set of durable entries, lets the main Agent save curated facts without periodic transcript mining, and gives the user direct control over every stored entry. Background Agents may propose entries, but the main Agent serializes writes.
design: Fork the pinned official Mem0 Pi integration and required TypeScript OSS core slice with full provenance. Use a Pi Stuff-owned Bun-native local store, schema versioning, atomic migration, backup and readable export. Default scope is the active project; global scope requires an explicit user action. Retrieved content is untrusted context. Save and update paths scan for credentials and instruction injection, verify scope before mutation, and never turn memory into policy. Use the shared full-width non-floating /memory Command Dialog plus Pi-native settings. Do not add a Memory statusline or duplicate state in Todo, Agents, or the footer.
acceptance_criteria: The package passes the repository owned-fork, exact dependency, public-data, tarball, and Aggregate checks. A real Pi session can save, recall, inspect, search, edit, delete, export, clear, and disable project memory through /memory and native settings. Same-name unrelated projects remain isolated; worktrees of one repository share the intended project scope; correction replaces or supersedes the right entry atomically; restart and schema migration preserve data; corrupted storage and unavailable retrieval degrade visibly without blocking normal work; context injection is bounded and source-marked; fresh-install behavior performs no telemetry, cloud call, model download, or other unexpected external transmission. The complete real Host and narrow-PTY matrix passes.
notes:
Superseded for the current implementation milestone by the maintainer-selected Magic Context trial. Preserve this work as a replacement candidate only; it does not block Goal, Web, MCP or completion.
Cancelled by the maintainer on 2026-08-05: Magic Context replaces the proposed Mem0 Capability. No Mem0 prototype or production package will be developed.
close_reason: Cancelled: Magic Context replaces the proposed Mem0 production Capability.

title: Improve Agent tool schema discoverability after real-model friction
description: Real-model daily-use dogfood initially produced multiple recoverable Agent validation errors: legacy background:true, an invalid status action, and mutually exclusive single/parallel shapes. The runtime correctly rejected them and the model recovered, so this does not block the UI-shell acceptance gate. Improve the public schema/descriptions only when the conditional-union or compatibility-alias design can remain precise, small, and model-visible without reviving retired workflow surfaces.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh real-model dogfood launches single and parallel Agents without schema-repair turns; invalid ambiguous shapes still fail closed with actionable errors; public Agent vocabulary and accepted current-session behavior remain unchanged; focused and real Pi tests pass.
notes:
2026-08-04: Claimed for strict public-seam TDD. Scope: improve model-visible Agent tool schema/validation for legacy background:true, invalid status actions, and ambiguous single/parallel shapes while preserving current vocabulary and fail-closed behavior. No retired chain/schedule/watchdog surfaces.
Confirmed test seam: the ToolDefinition registered by the public Extension API, exercised with Pi AI public validateToolArguments. Tests will inspect only model-visible description/parameters and observable validation outcomes, never private schema helpers.
RED evidence: `bun test test/agents/extension-root.test.ts --timeout 30000` => 8 pass, 1 fail. The registered Agent tool description lacked the exact-shape guidance (`Choose exactly one call shape`); current schema also still accepts a call containing both agent/task and tasks once the description assertion is bypassed.
GREEN evidence: public Extension seam test now passes 9/9 (89 expects). Its mixed single/parallel assertion requires Pi AI validateToolArguments to emit `must match exactly one schema in oneOf`, proving the registered schema executes the conditional contract. Broader focused set passes 23/23 (157 expects); full repository typecheck passed; Biome passes on all touched TypeScript files. README and patch Changeset added. Main Agent will run repository-wide gates and close.
Real-model closure evidence, 2026-08-04: fresh Pi/OpenAI model produced the single shape on its first attempt and completed a general-purpose child read successfully. A second fresh run produced exactly one parallel call with two tasks and no retired background field or schema-repair turn; async run b0437c26e5eb completed 2/2 successfully and returned @jczhang02/pi-stuff-ui and @jczhang02/pi-stuff-tools. Public-validator negative coverage continues to reject mixed single/parallel input with must match exactly one schema in oneOf.
close_reason: Model-visible single, parallel, and control shapes are explicit and mutually exclusive; public validation fails closed; focused/typecheck gates and fresh real-model single and parallel dogfood pass without repair turns.

title: Add semantic adjacent Tool grouping
description: Group adjacent low-impact exploration only after the certified Host exposes a public transcript transform or grouping seam. Do not patch Pi internals, mutate persisted messages, hide consequential operations, or infer grouping by floating overlays.
design: Keep the shipped one-row-per-operation baseline. A future implementation may collapse only adjacent low-impact operations, show at most two representative children plus an overflow count, and leave mutations/tests/builds/errors standalone. It must preserve local /tools addressing and model-visible results.
acceptance_criteria: Using only supported Pi 0.83 extension and TUI APIs, adjacent successful low-impact exploration calls collapse into one bounded display-only row with at most two representative Tool labels plus an overflow count. Mutations, tests/builds, ambiguous shell commands, and errors remain standalone; /tools retains every operation; model-visible results and session JSONL are unchanged. Real Pi PTYs certify live execution, /tools, reload, cold restart/resume, tree and compaction replay, focus, CJK width, narrow terminals, and bounded performance.
notes:
Blocked on Pi Host: 0.83.0 has no public adjacent transcript grouping/transform API.
2026-08-06 investigation: the certified Host already exposes a sufficient supported composition of public seams even without a transcript-transform API. Assistant message_end content identifies consecutive sibling tool calls; per-row renderers may return an empty Component, ToolRenderContext.invalidate can redraw earlier rows, and session_start can rebuild grouping metadata from SessionManager context. This permits display-only grouping without patching Host internals or rewriting persisted messages. Reopened for a real-PTY implementation.
Implementation in progress: Suite renderer state now composes public message_end/session lifecycle events with per-row self renderers and invalidate callbacks; no Host patch or persisted transcript rewrite is required.
Completed 2026-08-06 — Implemented on supported Pi 0.83 public seams: assistant message/session lifecycle builds display-only adjacency plans; per-row self renderers and invalidate collapse settled success rows without changing execution, model-visible results, or session JSONL. Conservative unbash parsing keeps mutations, tests/builds, ambiguous shell, configured prefixes, errors, and background handoffs standalone; /tools retains every operation.
Acceptance evidence: bun run check passed with 631 tests across 103 files plus Goal runtime suites, knip, generated/public checks, and standalone package certification. Real tmux PTYs passed live execution, /tools, reload, cold restart/resume, tree, compaction, CJK/narrow layout, background barriers, and transcript invariants. A 10,000-message / 20,000-call rebuild benchmark completed in 12.07 ms on the certification host. Implementation commit: cf12251.
close_reason: Implemented supported display-only adjacent exploration grouping with conservative standalone safeguards; certified on Pi 0.83 real PTYs and the complete repository gate.

title: Document the Suite domain and contributor contract
description: Create the repository instructions, domain glossary, architectural decision, tracker contract, contribution policy, security policy, and public project documentation.
acceptance_criteria: Engineering instructions are repository-scoped, domain terminology is canonical, the plugin boundary is explicit, and no engineering document becomes a Pi runtime resource.
close_reason: Repository instructions, domain glossary, ADR, tracker policy, contribution guide, and security documentation completed.

title: Revisit /doctor and default Skills
description: Future directions only: /doctor may explain which Suite capabilities loaded, which optional connections are unavailable, and what the user can do next; a small default Skill set may provide stable instructions for recurring coding workflows. Current package checks, startup errors, repository AGENTS.md instructions, and user-installed Skills remain the supported mechanisms.
design: Before implementation, decide what runtime facts the Host exposes safely, which checks are observation-only, how secrets are redacted, how degraded optional Capabilities report without creating a permanent health dashboard, and whether /doctor belongs in the Aggregate or a Capability. Default Skills need a separately reviewed inventory, clear trigger boundaries, provenance, versioning, conflicts with project instructions, and proof that they add repeatable behavior rather than generic prompts. Neither direction may silently modify user settings.
acceptance_criteria: The maintainer explicitly prioritizes /doctor, default Skills, or both; concrete inputs, outputs, redaction, failure, settings, update, provenance, and narrow-terminal behavior is decided; every proposed default Skill has a specific repeated workflow and tests; and separate implementation work maps are approved. Until then this decision remains deferred and authorizes no runtime resource, settings mutation, or permanent status display.
close_reason: Cancelled by maintainer decision: Pi Stuff will not ship /doctor or bundled default Skills.

title: Revisit rewind and recovery
description: Future direction only: the user may restore files, conversation state, or both to a known checkpoint after work goes wrong, with conflict detection and a way to undo the restoration. Current Git, session branching, and the destructive-command circuit breaker remain useful but do not constitute this full recovery Capability.
design: Before implementation, refresh the rewind package candidate and decide checkpoint timing, Git and non-Git files, untracked and ignored content, conversation linkage, background Agent ownership, conflicts with user edits, storage limits, pruning, crash consistency, undo, and disclosure of remote side effects that cannot be reversed. Recovery must never silently discard newer user work.
acceptance_criteria: The maintainer explicitly prioritizes the direction; checkpoint, preview, file-only, conversation-only, combined restore, conflict, crash, undo, pruning, child-Agent, and non-Git behavior is decided; irreversible remote effects are clearly out of scope; and a separate implementation work map is approved. Until then this decision remains deferred and authorizes no fork or automatic checkpoint writes.
notes: Maintainer decision, 2026-08-05: Rewind and checkpoint recovery are excluded from Pi Stuff. This supersedes the earlier 2026-08-03 session choice to include Rewind and the managed-write-only restoration design. Do not fork or implement a Rewind Capability; preserve the earlier records only as audit history.
close_reason: Maintainer explicitly removed Rewind and checkpoint recovery from the Pi Stuff product scope; this supersedes the earlier inclusion decision.

title: Revisit Loop and Cron session wakeups
description: Future direction only: a user may ask the current session to check again later or on a schedule, with a visible next wakeup and a way to cancel it. This is persistent scheduling infrastructure, not an Agent merely choosing to call tools repeatedly in the current turn.
design: Before implementation, refresh the Loop package candidate and decide one-shot versus recurring scope, timezone behavior, missed wakeups, busy-session coalescing, restart reconciliation, ownership after branch or session changes, permission and external-action boundaries, and cleanup. Loop and Cron must remain distinct from Goal completion, background processes, Todo, and system-wide cron unless the user explicitly selects a broader scope.
acceptance_criteria: The maintainer explicitly prioritizes the direction; schedule creation, listing, cancellation, wakeup, missed run, busy coalescing, restart, error, timezone, permission, and narrow-terminal behavior is decided; resource limits are testable; and a separate implementation work map is approved. Until then this decision remains deferred and authorizes no fork, scheduler, or automatic wakeup.
close_reason: Cancelled by maintainer decision: Pi Stuff will not ship Loop, Cron, scheduled wakeups, or a persistent daemon.

title: Revisit Plan mode and structured Ask
description: Future direction only: let the Agent perform read-only investigation, present a concrete implementation plan, and ask the user only for choices that materially change the result. If adopted, Plan and Ask must share the Pi Stuff Command Dialog and restore the editor draft and focus exactly. Existing model prose and ordinary clarification remain usable without this Capability.
design: Before implementation, re-audit the previously researched Plan-mode and Ask package candidates against the certified Host and owned-fork policy. Decide where read-only enforcement begins and ends, how approval transitions into implementation, what happens after rejection or revision, and how structured choices degrade when the Host is non-interactive. Do not treat an Agent writing a prose plan as evidence that this Capability already exists.
acceptance_criteria: The maintainer explicitly prioritizes the direction; refreshed package and license evidence exists; concrete Plan entry, edit, approve, reject, cancel, reload, permission, and narrow-terminal behavior is decided; and a separate implementation work map is approved. Until then this decision remains deferred and authorizes no fork or code.
close_reason: Cancelled by maintainer decision: Pi Stuff will not ship Plan mode or structured Ask; ordinary model planning and clarification remain sufficient.

title: Catalog deferred post-Memory capability directions
description: Keep the already discussed post-Memory directions visible without turning them into current commitments. These records describe possible daily-use outcomes and the unresolved gates for Plan and Ask, background shell and Monitor, Goal, Loop and Cron, rewind and recovery, Web reading and MCP connections, and /doctor with default Skills. They do not authorize a fork, source import, implementation, release scope, or delivery date.
design: Every child remains deferred until the maintainer explicitly selects it for product planning. When one is selected, refresh upstream, license, adoption, compatibility, and safety evidence; decide the concrete user-visible scope; create a separate implementation work map with dependencies and acceptance criteria; and preserve Pi as the Host plus the shared non-floating UI contract. Ordinary tasks that an Agent can already complete by composing tools are not separate Capabilities.
acceptance_criteria: All discussed directions exist as distinct deferred children with concrete usage descriptions, major decision gates, and explicit non-authorization language. None appears in bd ready or blocks the current Memory prototype or first-release preparation. Activating a direction requires an explicit maintainer priority decision and a new or updated implementation work map.
notes: Scope correction, 2026-08-05: ps-5cb.11.5 is no longer a deferred future direction. The maintainer explicitly excluded Rewind and checkpoint recovery; its earlier inclusion decision is superseded.
close_reason: The deferred catalog is retired: rejected directions are closed and Background Shell plus Monitor has been promoted into accepted implementation work.

title: Move BTW onto Pi's full host-managed side-call path when available
description: Pi 0.83 lets an extension resolve the active registered model and provider authentication without changing the transcript, but it does not expose a public host-managed model-call path that also remains transcript-free. The shipped BTW fork therefore performs the isolated provider call directly: it preserves the active model, registry authentication, tool-free context, independent cancellation, and transcript isolation, but it cannot inherit Pi Host provider lifecycle/context hooks or Host retry and transport settings. Revisit this task only when Pi exposes a suitable public seam; do not fork Pi or weaken BTW isolation to obtain it.
acceptance_criteria: BTW uses a public Pi Host API for an independent tools-disabled side question while preserving zero main-transcript writes, zero main-context writes, independent cancellation, active model/auth resolution, streaming, and current Command Dialog behavior. Provider lifecycle/context hooks plus Host retry/transport settings are exercised by real-host tests. No Pi fork is introduced.
